speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, how long have you had your wrist pain, and what does the pain feel like? Also, you mentioned a fever and skin lesions; can you describe the appearance and location of these lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI).

Thank you for those details; your recent sexual activity combined with the classic triad of migratory polyarthralgia (knee), tenosynovitis/wrist pain, and fever strongly suggests DGI caused by *Neisseria gonorrhoeae*. I need to confirm the severity of the wrist inflammation and check for joint effusion.
